title: Temp surge corridor capacity sampler — quick contacts & ownership
content:
Purpose:
A lightweight, ad-hoc spreadsheet to capture a 6-hour snapshot of regional surge corridors, quick owner handoffs, and immediate fallback routing suggestions.

Context and why this exists:
- Spike observed 2033-03-14 22:10 UTC: unexpected traffic shift from EU-west -> APAC-edge during model rollout.
- Need a fast, cross-team contact + capacity sampler to triage next 6 hours and feed into the automated fallback policy.
- This is intentionally minimal: one row per corridor, owner, immediate ask, short notes, and quick action (who pings pager / who can scale).

How to use:
1) Fill initial rows from telemetry (observability team export)
2) Product-ops calls the first contact in 'Owner' column if capacity < target
3) If owner unavailable, escalate to 'Alternate' then to 'Regional SRE'
4) Use 'Immediate action' to list 1-line fixes (increase pool, change route, toggle quantization).

Quick action checklist (top):
- [ ] Confirm telemetry window used (UTC 6h)
- [ ] Authorize temporary ramp (if needed) — product-ops
- [ ] Post summary to #ops-surge and @oncall (first 6h status updates every 60m)

Table (one-line rows, paste into the sheet view):
Corridor | Region pair | Current qps | Target qps | Headroom % | Owner | Alternate | Regional SRE | Immediate action (1-line) | Notes
APAC-edge -> EU-west | APAC->EU | 4200 | 2500 | -68% | Jonah Li | Marta Rodriguez | Ethan Clarke | shift-route to eu-fallback-02; increase apac-burst by +2 | model variant A has higher mem
EU-west -> US-central | EU->US | 1800 | 2000 | -10% | Marta Rodriguez | Aisha Patel | Priya Shah | toggle dedupe cache; evaluate prefix-cache miss | trending down, watch 30m
US-central -> APAC-edge | US->APAC | 900 | 1200 | -25% | Ethan Clarke | Jonah Li | Carlos Mendez | enable quant-profile-3 for short seq; spin small unit | low errors but latency spike
EU-west intra | EU region | 300 | 500 | -40% | Aisha Patel | Priya Shah | Marta Shah | raise reserved capacity by +1; hold canary | customer-critical route

Quick glossary:
- Corridor: logical route pair we observed as contended
- Headroom %: (current - target)/target * 100 (negative means over target)
- Immediate action: what a human can do in <15m

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Who owns the follow-up to make fallback permanent? (PR/Config change)
- Can we add this corridor to the routing-health dashboard? (obs ticket created)
- Should we bake 'owner' into oncall rotation for top-5 corridors?

Notes to self (Aisha):
- If escalation goes to Product oncall, ping @product-leads and include the small CSV export (columns: corridor,current,target,owner,action).
- Capture outcome of every Immediate action as simple tags: success/partial/fail. Add a 1-line postmortem if fail.

Recent edits log (manual):
- 2033-03-15 09:12 UTC — initial draft (Aisha)
- 2033-03-16 02:40 UTC — added EU->US row (Marta)
- 2033-03-21 17:05 UTC — updated headroom calc note and added quick checklist (Jonah)

Slack quickcopy for #ops-surge (paste):
"Heads up: temporary surge corridor sampler live (sheet): temp-surge-corridor-capacity-sampler-mar-2033. Current top corridor APAC->EU over target by 68%. Jonah Li taking first action (route shift). Updates every 60m. Linked artifacts: CONFLUENCE-4672 JIRA-OPS-1218"

End of doc.
